title: Study links higher AI exposure with a larger education wage premium
friendlyTitle: Early research links AI-heavy jobs with a bigger education pay gap
summary: An observational study combining US labour data from 2015–2025 with an occupational AI-exposure index finds the clearest post-2023 association in returns to education rather than experience. Among knowledge workers, the estimated college-premium difference between high- and low-AI occupations rose to about 14.7% by 2025, while earnings results were not consistently significant.
friendlySummary: A study found that college education was linked with a larger pay advantage in US knowledge jobs that use more AI. The study did not find a clear, consistent effect on total earnings.
whyItMatters: The findings point toward AI complementing formal education in exposed knowledge work, but they do not prove that AI caused the wage pattern. Workers and employers should read this as an early signal to pair tool skills with domain knowledge, not as a settled forecast.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This suggests that subject knowledge and education may still matter a lot when people use AI. The research shows a link, not proof that AI caused the change.
